editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-healthcare city of about 1.3 million. Its retail is heavy on coaching & training and banks & atms, and thin on desserts, sweets & ice cream and grocery & daily needs — and 30% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 53% of Mumbai's. 12.63 chain outlets per lakh residents against 23.76 in Mumbai; 32 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 31, Reliance Digital 15, Domino's 12.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 3.7% (Mumbai 2.2%); malls & department stores 0.5% (Mumbai 0.4%); desserts & sweets 0.6% (Mumbai 1.1%); other services 6.4% (Mumbai 8.4%). Raw counts would mislead because Mumbai is mapped more completely (70,423 places against 12,813), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 3 zones hold 30% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Panchvati alone has about 249,000 residents and 112 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is more concentrated than in Mumbai. 47% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Mumbai 38%). The largest cores are H P T College (1,213 places) and Panchvati (988).

The widest brand gaps against Mumbai. Café Coffee Day 10 outlets vs 169; Domino's 12 outlets vs 115; Subway 2 outlets vs 81. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Mumbai, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Panchvati and Ambad A.S are the largest zones by residents (249,000 and 153,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 47% of all commercial places, and H P T College alone lists 1,213.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. H P T College holds 40 of the 167 tracked chain outlets, and Cidco Colony adds 21.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. H P T College and Panchvati lead on education places (163 and 126, with 90 and 46 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Panchvati and Gandhi Nagar. The blue cores include H P T College.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (70,423 places in Mumbai against 12,813 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Mumbai; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Mumbai, Nashik's mapped places over-index on automotive (3.7% vs 2.2%), malls & department stores (0.5% vs 0.4%), healthcare (11.8% vs 8.7%) and under-index on desserts & sweets (0.6% vs 1.1%), other services (6.4% vs 8.4%), grocery & daily needs (1.4% vs 1.9%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 167 outlets of 32 tracked national brands within 8 km — 12.63 per lakh residents against Mumbai's 23.76 (1266 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Mumbai are Café Coffee Day (10 vs 169); Domino's (12 vs 115); Subway (2 vs 81). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Mumbai's, so low means thin by Mumbai's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Nashik's age mix against Mumbai: children (0–14) 27.9% vs 19.9%, 15–24 19.8% vs 19.7%, working age 43.9% vs 52.0%, 60+ 8.4% vs 8.4%. Under-25s are 48% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 5.6% of mapped places against 7.0% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 12 (Mumbai 115), Pizza Hut 7 (Mumbai 53), KFC 5 (Mumbai 38), Burger King 5 (Mumbai 34).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.4% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 10 (Mumbai 169), Starbucks 1 (Mumbai 64).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.6% of mapped places against 1.1% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 2 (Mumbai 57), Naturals 1 (Mumbai 18), Cream Stone 1 (Mumbai 0).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.4% of mapped places against 1.9% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 5 (Mumbai 18), Big Bazaar 4 (Mumbai 8), DMart 2 (Mumbai 24), Easyday 1 (Mumbai 0). No mapped outlet in either city: More, Vishal Mega Mart.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.0% of mapped places against 1.3% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 31 (Mumbai 45), Wellness Forever 10 (Mumbai 17), MedPlus 1 (Mumbai 1). No mapped outlet in either city: Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.5% of mapped places against 4.8% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Raymond 6 (Mumbai 40), Titan 6 (Mumbai 32), Reliance Trends 5 (Mumbai 20), Bata 5 (Mumbai 52). No mapped outlet in either city: V-Mart.
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.8% of mapped places against 7.8% in Mumbai — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.8% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.8% of mapped places against 4.4% in Mumbai — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
